newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to bar cars from Paris to counter smog.
newsitem.headline: France to bar cars from Paris to counter smog.

text.p: France's government said on Tuesday it would impose draconian controls on driving cars in Paris at times of high pollution as breezes dispersed a latest shroud of smog stifling the capital.

Environment Minister Corinne Lepage said that Prime Minister Alain Juppe had decided to introduce a system barring half of all vehicles from Paris and suburbs served by the Metro underground railway when pollution reached dangerous levels.
Under the system, only vehicles with an even number at the start of their license plate would be allowed to drive on one day, those with even numbers the next, she told the National Assembly.

Apart from emergency vehicles like ambulances and fire engines, buses, taxis, electric vehicles and cars used for driving pools would be exempt. Pollution reaches an "alert" level only once every few years in Paris.
Light winds on Tuesday dispersed a build-up of smog over the capital caused by a combination of car exhausts, unseasonably hot weather and stagnant air.
Air quality rose to "mediocre" from "bad" but never fell to the levels that would trigger driving restrictions under the new plan.

Police decreed stricter speed limits in the Paris area on Tuesday in a bid to counter the pollution. Drivers also faced snarl-ups because of a demonstration by Renault car workers protesting at job cuts.
Authorities lowered the limit from 80 kph (50 mph) to 60 kmh (37 mph) on the capital's ring road, and from 70 kph (44 mph) to 50 kph (30 mph) on express riverbank roads through the city.
Paris mayor Jean Tiberi made residential parking free of charge to encourage locals to use buses and the underground metro railway until pollution levels return to normal.
